title: Smart rollback calibration for multi-metric rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an automated rollback calibration system that derives safe, context-aware thresholds for canary/A-B/shadow rollouts from historical traffic, synthetic experiments, and continuous evaluation. The goal is to replace brittle static thresholds with a multi-signal, tunable scoring model that triggers rollbacks (or safe pauses) on regressions in latency, error rate, token cost, or throughput while minimizing false positives and unnecessary rollbacks.
motivation: We frequently see two failure modes during model rollouts: (1) overly sensitive thresholds cause noisy rollbacks for transient spikes, interrupting deployments and increasing toil; (2) static thresholds miss regressions that degrade customer experience or cost. A calibrated, traffic-aware rollback policy reduces risk, shortens detection time for real regressions, and avoids unnecessary rollbacks.
goals: (1) Define a multi-metric rollback scoring function combining p50/p95 latency, 5xx/error rate, token_cost_per_1k, and throughput. (2) Implement automated threshold tuning per traffic segment (interactive vs background vs high-throughput batch). (3) Integrate calibration into canary ramp and A/B experiments with shadow verification. (4) Provide console UI and CLI controls for override and audit logs.
non_goals: Model training improvements, kernel-level optimizations, dedicated capacity autoscaler changes. This work focuses on rollout decision logic and tooling around existing metrics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Canary rollouts using the new policy must detect a synthetic regression (artificial latency injection) within configured SLO windows and trigger a rollback automatically in the staging environment. 2) The policy must expose a tunable sensitivity parameter and per-segment thresholds visible in Console. 3) Add end-to-end tests that simulate transient spikes and sustained regressions; false positive rate must be <5% on historical traces. 4) Rollback events must include an audit record with contributing signals and scored reasons in the timeline.
implementation_notes: Plan: (A) Build a scoring service that ingests time-series windows (30s/2m/5m) and computes z-scores vs historical baselines per metric. (B) Use weighted aggregation into an overall rollback score with a configurable sensitivity multiplier. (C) Add segmentation: derive baseline distributions per route/model/version, region, and traffic class. (D) Add a simulation harness that replays historical traffic and synthetic regressions to autotune weights and sensitivity. (E) Integrate the scoring service with rollout controller: score evaluations run at each ramp step and can issue PAUSE/ROLLBACK/CONTINUE decisions with reasoning metadata.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting thresholds to historical data causing missed new failure modes. Mitigation: include synthetic injection scenarios and holdout windows during tuning.
Risk: High-cardinality segmentation increases storage/compute. Mitigation: tier segments (global, model, route) and apply sampling/decay for low-traffic segments.
Risk: Increased time-to-decision due to complex scoring. Mitigation: optimize window sizes, precompute baselines, and cache scores for common routes.
Risk: DBA/ops pushback on automated rollbacks. Mitigation: provide conservative defaults, adjustable sensitivity, and clear audit trails for each action.

Risk: False positives during release-related load tests. Mitigation: auto-detect synthetic test flags (from CI headers) and suppress automatic rollback in flagged windows or require manual confirmation.

Risk: Interactions with existing fallback policies causing oscillations. Mitigation: add cooldown windows and state machine guards to prevent rapid flip-flopping; record decisions in timeline for debugging.
metrics_to_monitor: Detection latency (time from regression injection to rollback decision)
False positive rate on historical traces
Mean token cost delta after deployment
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and baseline stats. Integration tests for segment baseline retrieval. Simulation: replay 30 days of historical traffic with injected regressions (latency bump, 5xx spike, token cost increase). Staging e2e: blue-green canary runs with controlled injections. A/B: run parallel rollouts where one arm uses the legacy static thresholds and the other uses the smart-calibrated policy; compare detection timeliness and false positives.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy scoring service behind feature flag and run in passive mode (log-only) for 2 weeks. Phase 2: enable advisory mode (controller suggests actions but does not execute). Phase 3: enable automatic PAUSE (not rollback) for low-sensitivity. Phase 4: enable auto-rollback with conservative sensitivity in non-prod, then ramp to prod after 4 weeks and observed FP <5%.
rollback_policy_examples: Example A (conservative): require score > 0.9 for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows OR 5xx rate > 1% sustained for 5 minutes => PAUSE then human review
Example B (aggressive): score > 0.7 for 3 consecutive windows OR token_cost increase > 20% for 2 minutes => ROLLBACK
Example C (segment-aware): high-throughput batch routes use higher throughput weight and tolerate p95 increases up to 25% if token_cost decreases by >10%
